varieties.name: Allegheny
varieties.summary: Peterson Pawpaws release; smaller fruit with a milder, citrus-tinged flavor. Highly productive, early-ripening.
varieties.description: Peterson Pawpaws release. Smaller fruit (6–12 oz) with a milder, citrus-tinged flavor. Highly productive — can need thinning to avoid overcropping — and ripens early in the season.
notes: Sold out at Stark Bro's (since Sep 20) and at Perry Paw Paws. The Ty Ty listing is orderable now for a projected Jan 25, 2027 shipment.

varieties.name: Benny's Favorite
varieties.summary: Bred by Jerry Lehman (Terre Haute, IN), a Prolific x Sam Norris-15 cross. Refined classic pawpaw flavor, repeat Ohio Pawpaw Festival winner.
varieties.description: Bred by Jerry Lehman of Terre Haute, IN, a cross of Prolific × Sam Norris-15. Prized for refined, classic pawpaw flavor and creamy texture; a repeat Ohio Pawpaw Festival award-winner. Needs a long, hot season.

varieties.name: Cricket Hill Garden Select
varieties.summary: Cricket Hill Garden's own in-house selection. No independent breeding history found; sold only under this house name.
varieties.description: A house selection sold only by Cricket Hill Garden under its own name, at a notably lower price than its other pawpaw listings. No independent breeding history or parentage was found — likely an unnamed-seedling-grade tree given a shop name rather than a documented cultivar.

varieties.name: Dale
varieties.summary: Described by Rock Bridge Trees as a contest-winning, large-fruited selection. Little independent documentation found.
varieties.description: A name never logged anywhere on this page before. Rock Bridge Trees describes it as a large-fruited pawpaw that has won several fruit contests; little independent documentation was found, so treat the description as the nursery's own.
awards: Several fruit contests (per Rock Bridge Trees)

varieties.name: Green River Belle
varieties.summary: Marketed as a Kentucky heirloom endorsed by breeder Neal Peterson. Medium fruit, subtle cinnamon aftertaste. Limited independent documentation.
varieties.description: Marketed as a Kentucky heirloom pawpaw endorsed by breeder Neal Peterson. Medium fruit with a subtle cinnamon aftertaste, said to set fruit well through difficult spring weather. Limited independent documentation beyond nursery listings.

varieties.name: Halvin
varieties.summary: Wild-origin selection from southwestern Iowa. Large fruit, ripens 2-3 weeks after Shenandoah; possibly more leaf-spot resistant.
varieties.description: Wild-origin selection from southwestern Iowa (Bedford area). Large fruit, ripening two to three weeks after Shenandoah; may show more resistance to phyllosticta leaf spot than most named cultivars.

varieties.name: Honeydew
varieties.summary: An England's Orchard freestone introduction (with Marshmallow and Cantaloupe) from Richmond, KY. Large fruit, easy seed removal, early-to-mid ripening.
varieties.description: One of three England's Orchard "freestone" introductions from Richmond, KY (with Marshmallow and Cantaloupe). Large fruit with easy seed removal, ripening early-to-mid season.

varieties.name: IXL
varieties.summary: Long-standing heirloom selection, origin undocumented. Very-late-season ripening, complex yellow-fleshed fruit.
varieties.description: A long-standing heirloom selection with limited documented origin history. Known for very-late-season ripening and complex, yellow-fleshed fruit.

varieties.name: Jerry's Big Girl
varieties.summary: Bred by the late Jerry Lehman from thousands of Terre Haute, IN seedlings. Very large fruit, heavy production, multiple Ohio Pawpaw Festival wins.
varieties.description: Bred by the late Jerry Lehman from thousands of seedlings on his Terre Haute, IN farm. Very large fruit (10–14 oz, some over a pound) with heavy production; won Best Taste and Biggest Pawpaw at the Ohio Pawpaw Festival.
awards: Best Taste and Biggest Pawpaw, Ohio Pawpaw Festival

varieties.name: Kentucky Champion
varieties.summary: Origin undocumented. Yellow-orange flesh, vigorous tree, ripens early. Sold as 'KY Champion' at Beautiful Beginnings, same cultivar.
varieties.description: Origin undocumented; yellow-orange flesh on a vigorous, moderately productive tree. Ripens early — plant with another early cultivar for pollination.
notes: Sold out at Beautiful Beginnings (as “KY Champion”) since Sep 24 — Rock Bridge Trees is now the only listing. Perry Paw Paws sold out earlier.

varieties.name: KSU Atwood
varieties.summary: Kentucky State University release (2009). Large, highly productive fruit with more leaf-spot resistance than most; ripens early-mid.
varieties.description: Kentucky State University release, originated in Maryland and introduced in 2009. Large, highly productive fruit with more resistance to phyllosticta leaf spot than most cultivars; ripens early-to-mid season.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now). Logee's, previously listed as unavailable, now shows this cultivar in stock and buyable online.

varieties.name: KSU Benson
varieties.summary: Kentucky State University release (2016). Large, round fruit, rich flavor, low seed weight; highly productive.
varieties.description: Kentucky State University release (2016). Large, fairly round fruit with rich flavor and low seed weight; highly productive and resistant to phyllosticta leaf spot.

varieties.name: KSU Chappell
varieties.summary: Kentucky State University release (2018). Large freestone fruit, fastest-growing KSU variety, somewhat prone to cracking.
varieties.description: Kentucky State University release (2018). Large, freestone fruit with medium flavor. The fastest-growing KSU variety, but somewhat prone to cracking and less disease-resistant than its siblings.
notes: Perry Paw Paws sold out since yesterday (moved to the Watchlist). Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: KSU Dunnigan
varieties.summary: Kentucky State University pawpaw-program release (7-1); still building a track record.
varieties.description: A Kentucky State University pawpaw-program release (selection 7-1), still building a track record. Sold out at Beautiful Beginnings and Peaceful Heritage as of the last check — now orderable at Rock Bridge Trees (restock, per the † caveat below).

varieties.name: KSU Pomper's Choice
varieties.summary: Kentucky State University release (2025); freestone, outstanding tropical flavor.
varieties.description: A Kentucky State University release (2025); freestone fruit with a notably tropical flavor. Sold out at Beautiful Beginnings and Peaceful Heritage as of the last check — now orderable at Rock Bridge Trees (restock, per the † caveat below).

varieties.name: KY Legend “Titan”
varieties.summary: Traces to Jerry Lehman seed given to Cliff England c. 2010, a Jerry's Big Girl x Jerry's Delight cross. Very large fruit, pineapple flavor, can split in heavy rain.
varieties.description: Traces to experimental Jerry Lehman seed given to Cliff England around 2010, a Jerry's Big Girl × Jerry's Delight cross. Very large fruit (avg. 360g, up to 800g) with pineapple-like flavor and very low seed weight; can split in heavy rain. Rock Bridge Trees, which also lists it, instead credits selection to grower Woody Walker — the two nurseries' histories don't fully agree.
notes: Sold out at Beautiful Beginnings since Sep 24.

varieties.name: Lehman's Chiffon
varieties.summary: Bred by Jerry Lehman, a Prolific x Sunflower cross. Abundant creamy fruit, pleasant sweet aftertaste. Limited public detail.
varieties.description: Bred by Jerry Lehman, a Prolific × Sunflower cross. Abundant crops of creamy-textured fruit with a pleasant sweet aftertaste. Limited public detail beyond nursery listings.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: Lehman's Delight (275-48)
varieties.summary: Bred by the late Jerry Lehman. Twice won and twice runner-up for Biggest Pawpaw at the Ohio Pawpaw Festival.
varieties.description: Bred by the late Jerry Lehman of Terre Haute, IN. Twice won and twice placed runner-up for Biggest Pawpaw at the Ohio Pawpaw Festival; ripens mid-to-late season.
awards: Biggest Pawpaw, Ohio Pawpaw Festival (2 wins, 2 runner-up)
notes: Sold out at Beautiful Beginnings since Sep 24.

varieties.name: Mango
varieties.summary: Wild selection from Tifton, GA (1970). Vigorous, soft-textured, good flavor -- doesn't actually taste of mango.
varieties.description: Wild selection from Tifton, GA (1970). Vigorous tree, soft-textured fruit with good flavor — the name is a bit of a misnomer, since it doesn't actually taste of mango.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: Maria's Joy (166-13)
varieties.summary: A Davis x Prolific cross from Indiana. Large fruit, once a standout, now mixed grower reviews.
varieties.description: A Davis × Prolific cross from Indiana. Large fruit; once considered a standout, now gets mixed reviews from growers.

varieties.name: Marshmallow
varieties.summary: England's Orchard freestone introduction, Richmond KY -- the sweetest of its three siblings (with Honeydew, Cantaloupe).
varieties.description: An England's Orchard introduction from Richmond, KY — the sweetest of its three freestone siblings (with Honeydew and Cantaloupe). Large fruit, early-to-mid ripening.

varieties.name: Mitchell
varieties.summary: Wild-collected selection, Franklin County IL, documented in KSU records. Cream flesh, airy texture, excellent flavor.
varieties.description: Wild-collected selection from Franklin County, IL, documented in KSU's cultivar records. Cream-colored flesh, large round fruit with an airy texture and excellent flavor.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: NC-1
varieties.summary: Davis x Overleese cross, Ontario 1976. Strong high-acetogenin flavor; below-average yields, more disease-prone.
varieties.description: Bred from a Davis × Overleese cross in Ontario, Canada (1976). Strong, high-acetogenin flavor and dark foliage; ripens early-to-mid season but yields below average and is more disease-prone than most named cultivars.
notes: Lost its cheapest, fully-confirmed listing this run: sold out at Edible Landscaping and no longer confirmed at Stark Bro's (both since Sep 24), so the best landed cost jumped from a confirmed ~$59 to an estimated ~$93–103. Also sold out at Perry Paw Paws since Sep 20. A newly-found Trusty Farms listing (see Watchlist) may reopen a cheaper option once its stock is confirmed.

varieties.name: Nyomi's Delicious
varieties.summary: Discovered in a Berea, KY garden, introduced by Cliff England. Sweet, citrusy, no muskiness; vigorous and disease-resistant.
varieties.description: Discovered in a Berea, KY garden and introduced by nurseryman Cliff England. Exceptionally sweet with bright citrus notes and no muskiness; large fruit in clusters of four to five, vigorous, disease-resistant and cold-hardy.

varieties.name: Overleese
varieties.summary: Wild find, Overleese family yard, Rushville IN c. 1950. Mild flavor, stores well, parent of Shenandoah.
varieties.description: A wild selection found in the Overleese family yard, Rushville, IN (c. 1950). Large fruit borne in clusters, mild flavor, good seed-to-pulp ratio, and stores better than most — the parent of Shenandoah.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: PA Golden #3
varieties.summary: Pennsylvania Golden group, selected by John Gordon from wild PA/NY trees. Golden watery flesh, very high-yielding, stores poorly.
varieties.description: Part of the Pennsylvania Golden group selected by John Gordon from wild Pennsylvania and Amherst, NY trees. Golden, watery flesh with a strong wild-pawpaw flavor; very high-yielding but stores poorly.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: Pennsylvania Golden
varieties.summary: Likely the same Pennsylvania Golden clonal family under a shortened name; this nursery doesn't specify the numbered selection.
varieties.description: Likely the same Pennsylvania Golden clonal family sold under a shortened name — see Pennsylvania Golden 4 above for the group's traits. This nursery doesn't specify which numbered selection it's growing.

varieties.name: Pennsylvania Golden 4
varieties.summary: Pennsylvania Golden group (PA Golden #1-4), selected by John Gordon. Smaller fruit but can yield 25-50 lb/tree.
varieties.description: Part of the Pennsylvania Golden group (PA Golden #1–4) selected by John Gordon from wild Pennsylvania and Amherst, NY trees. Smaller fruit with a lower pulp-to-skin ratio, but can yield 25–50 lb per tree.

varieties.name: Potomac
varieties.summary: Peterson Pawpaws release, Boyce VA. Large fleshy fruit, strong sweet flavor, upright fast-growing precocious tree.
varieties.description: Peterson Pawpaws release from Boyce, VA. Large, fleshy fruit with a strong sweet flavor on an upright, fast-growing, precocious tree — somewhat prone to cracking.
notes: Perry Paw Paws sold out since yesterday (moved to the Watchlist).

varieties.name: Prima
varieties.summary: A Sunflower seedling selected in Italy by Domenico Montanari. Mango-apricot flavor, reliably self-fertile, late-ripening.
varieties.description: A Sunflower seedling selected in Italy by Domenico Montanari. Mango-apricot-pineapple flavor with vanilla-marshmallow notes; one of the only reliably self-fertile cultivars, but late-ripening — not suited to short northern seasons.
notes: Sold out at Perry Paw Paws as of Sep 25; also sold as “Prima 1216” at Beautiful Beginnings (sold out).

varieties.name: Prolific
varieties.summary: Corwin Davis-orchard selection, Bellevue MI (1980s). Mild flavor, thick texture; fruit quality considered inferior.
varieties.description: A Corwin Davis-orchard selection from Bellevue, MI (1980s). Mild flavor and thick texture, but fruit quality is considered inferior with a possible bitter aftertaste.
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now).

varieties.name: Quaker Delight
varieties.summary: An Ohio Pawpaw Festival prize-winner. Medium fruit in clusters, creamy texture, ripens earlier than many cultivars.
varieties.description: An Ohio Pawpaw Festival prize-winner. Medium fruit in clusters, creamy texture and mild pleasant flavor, ripening earlier than many named cultivars.

varieties.name: Rebecca's Gold
varieties.summary: Corwin Davis selection, Bellevue MI (1974). Very late-ripening, below-average flavor; grown mainly for its late season and hardiness.
varieties.description: A Corwin Davis-orchard selection from Bellevue, MI (1974). Very late-ripening with below-average flavor by most accounts — valued mainly for extending the season and for hardiness, not for eating quality.
notes: Was Watchlist-only (sold out at Restoring Eden and listed in West Farm's 2027 lineup); today it's the first time this cultivar has actually been buyable anywhere on this tracker. Restoring Eden's per-plant shipping formula (a size-based rate plus $5/plant) isn't published as an NJ figure, so the shipping above is an estimate.

varieties.name: Regulus
varieties.summary: A Shenandoah x Susquehanna cross. Large fruit, excellent flavor, low seed ratio, extremely heavy-bearing.
varieties.description: A Shenandoah × Susquehanna cross. Large fruit, excellent flavor, low seed ratio, and extremely heavy-bearing.

varieties.name: SAA Zimmerman
varieties.summary: Selected by John Gordon (Amherst NY, 1982). Large yellow fruit, few seeds, suckers readily, hardy zones 5-9.
varieties.description: Selected as a seedling from G.A. Zimmerman-collection seed by John Gordon, Amherst, NY (1982). Large fruit, yellow skin and flesh, few seeds; suckers readily from the base and is hardy across zones 5–9.

varieties.name: Shenandoah
varieties.summary: Peterson Pawpaws release, seedling of Overleese from Boyce VA. Mild fragrant-sweet flavor, few seeds, precocious.
varieties.description: Peterson Pawpaws release, a Boyce, VA seedling of Overleese. One of the mildest, most fragrant-sweet cultivars — custardy texture, very few seeds, precocious and early-to-mid ripening.
notes: No longer confirmed in stock at Stark Bro's since Sep 24 (its own sold-out list wasn't fully disclosed). Sold out at Perry Paw Paws and Restoring Eden; Cricket Hill lists it as coming soon. Logee's, previously unavailable, now shows this cultivar buyable online. The Ty Ty listing is orderable now for a projected Jan 25, 2027 shipment.

varieties.name: Sunflower
varieties.summary: Wild selection near Chanute, KS (1970). Self-fertile, large butter-colored fruit, can have a bitter aftertaste. Shrubs & Trees Depot credits it with a 2010 Ohio Pawpaw Festival win.
varieties.description: A wild selection found near Chanute, KS (1970). Self-fertile, with large, butter-colored fruit — flavorful, though some fruit can carry a bitter aftertaste; mid-to-late ripening. Shrubs & Trees Depot's listing credits it with winning first prize at the 2010 Ohio Pawpaw Festival.
awards: 1st prize, 2010 Ohio Pawpaw Festival (per Shrubs & Trees Depot)
notes: Hidden Springs ships in its Nov–Apr season (pre-order now). Sold out at Restoring Eden. A newly-found source, Burnt Ridge Nursery & Orchards (WA), also lists a grafted Sunflower and ships, but only seed pricing was visible this pass — see Watchlist, it'll move up here once the tree price is confirmed.

varieties.name: Susquehanna
varieties.summary: Peterson Pawpaws release, Boyce VA (patented 2004). Large fruit, very low seed weight, top flavor scores.
varieties.description: Peterson Pawpaws release from Boyce, VA (patented 2004). Large fruit, very low seed weight, firm texture and top flavor scores — though relatively disease-prone.

notes: Grafted 1-gal, walk-in retail only (Th–Mon, 9:30–6) — no mail order. At a firm $39 with no shipping cost, this is the cheapest confirmed named pawpaw on the whole page, if you're willing to make the drive.
